_notes: M4 marketing ladder, in order. kind: boost (attendance x (1 + boost) for `days`), spike (a one-day boost), floor (weekday attendance floor while active), perk (one-time permanent effect, stored in state.perks), memberships (one-time launch of the season pass; mechanics in balance.marketing.memberships). stack: true means several copies can run at once (up to balance.marketing.stack_max); otherwise only the strongest active boost counts and the same campaign cannot be bought again while it runs. unlock: min_species (living species), min_rating (park stars), requires_facility { id: tier }, requires_dinos. lesson: the one-line economics lesson shown on the card and in the ticker.

campaigns.name: Flyers
campaigns.lesson: Cheap and local. The first dollar of marketing is the best one you will ever spend.

campaigns.name: Radio Spot
campaigns.lesson: Reach costs money. Radio only pays back if the park has more than one thing to see.

campaigns.name: TV Spot
campaigns.lesson: Big reach, big bill. Check the what-if: a boost is worth nothing above your parking cap.

campaigns.name: Social Media Campaign
campaigns.lesson: Small, short and stackable. Many little pushes can beat one big one, but each one still has to pay for itself.

campaigns.name: Influencer Visit
campaigns.lesson: A one-day crowd is only worth what your gate and parking can hold. Capacity turns hype into money.

campaigns.name: School Field-Trip Program
campaigns.lesson: Schools book on weekdays and in every season. A guaranteed floor smooths the quiet days that sink a park.

campaigns.name: Online Ticketing
campaigns.lesson: Buy once, benefit forever. Easier buying makes visitors a little less price-sensitive, every day, for good.

campaigns.name: Memberships / Season Pass
campaigns.lesson: Steady money instead of ticket-by-ticket money. Members pay every quarter, and they leave when the park slips.
